key_insight: The minimum energy needed to trigger turbulence in pipe flow decreases as Re^{-3}, while the perturbation structure becomes more localized and thinner with thickness scaling as Re^{-1/3}.
engineering_relevance: This scaling law helps estimate disturbance tolerance and transition thresholds for pipelines and internal flows at high Reynolds number.
method: Variational optimization of nonlinear perturbations to laminar pipe flow
Track growth through Orr, oblique-wave interaction, and lift-up phases
Analyze how optimal structure and transition threshold scale up to Re<=5000
evidence_signal: The abstract reports computed nonlinear optimal perturbations and scaling trends across Reynolds numbers up to 5000, showing consistent threshold behavior and phase-dependent energy gains.
watch_item: The result is based on an idealized pipe-flow model and Reynolds numbers up to 5000, so extrapolation to more complex geometries or higher-Re regimes should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Scaling of the minimal energy for turbulence transition in pipe flow
